newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia president warns on privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia president warns on privatisation.

text.p: Mongolia's president, standard bearer of the former communists, said on Friday he backed privatisation but wanted to ensure it proceeded fairly and did not harm national security.
Natsagiin Bagabandi also told his first news conference since his election in May he was unhappy with the government's reliance on public auctions to sell off state assets.
"I will work along the policy of ...speedy privatisation and developing an economy which is supported by private property," Bagabandi said.
"The National Security Council should consider extremely carefully whether the outcome of privatisation... would be against our national security," he said.

The president, who was swept into office on a tide of dissatisfaction over the policies of the reformist Democratic Union Coalition government, has aroused fears he would slow Mongolia's plan to promote privatisation and reduce the state's role in the economy.
Bagabandi was elected as the candidate of the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party, the ex-communists, but he relinquished his party membership before his inauguration to conform with local law.
The Mongolian parliament, which is controlled by the reformists, urged the government on Thursday to speed up privatisation of big state companies.
Mongolia has held regular public auctions, selling off mainly small shops and offices. Most of the buyers have been local companies but the auctions are open to foreigners.

Bagabandi said he would rather see revenues from such sales go to new state investments and not "flow out through a hole in the pot" of the state budget. He gave no further details of his view of the direction of the privatisation drive.
